Welcome everyone. Point to the bus: Lessons 1 to 4 are ticked. Today the bus moves on to Lesson 5: What's out there? Finding, recording and talking about services and activities. The first part of this deck looks back at all four lessons, then it introduces Lesson 5 before students get the worksheet. Allow about 30 to 40 minutes.

Point to each lesson. Ask: "What did we do in Lesson 1?" Let students answer, then click the card to show the "can do" line. Keep it quick, about 5 minutes. Lesson 5 is the last step before Part 3: choosing services and activities, filling every row of the research table, naming sources, and practising both halves of the discussion.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Make the link clear. Lesson 4 was about your own area. Lesson 5 is about the places in it: which ones are community services and which are recreation activities, where they are, what to write in each row of the research table, how to name a source, and how to talk with the teacher about one service and one activity. After Lesson 5, students are ready for Part 3.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Walk the route with the class. Click a stop to show what it is about. Lesson 5 has 11 stops and 34 activities: talk first (listening), everyday expressions, Say it (phone numbers, emails and a polite voice), grammar (the simple present, how often and time words), where is it (address, location and directions), what counts (the directory), the research table, sources, plan your discussion, a practice discussion, and check your learning.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs decide for each picture: community service (helps people with a need), recreation activity (free time, fun, fitness, friends) or business (sells things). Click Show. Ask: "Which two community services could you choose for your project?" This previews Stop 6. Remind students to choose two different places: a book club inside the library is the same place as the library.

Say numbers and emails

How do Australians say these? Try first, then click.
Emergency
000
Practice email
swim@wavertonbaths.com.au
Practice number
(02) 5550 7782
!000 is triple zero. In an email, @ is at and a full stop is dot.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
The class says each number together first. Then click the card to show the words, and say it yourself (the computer voice is a back-up only). Point out the groups and the short stop between groups, "oh" for 0 and "double" for two the same. For emails: @ is "at" and a full stop is "dot". The research table asks for the phone number and the email. 000 is real; the other two are practice details from the worksheet. This previews Stop 3.

Where is it?

At, on or in? Say it with your partner first. Then click the blank.
1
The centre is 18 Falcon Street.
2
It's Falcon Street, Crows Nest.
3
It's the corner of Falcon Street and Miller Street.
4
Walk to Miller Street. Turn right and Falcon Street.
Address order: number, street, suburb, state, postcode.  18 Falcon Street, Crows Nest NSW 2065
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs say each sentence first, then click the blanks. at + a number, on + a street, in + a suburb. Ask: "Where is your favourite place? What's it near?" The teacher asks these questions in Part 3. This previews Stop 5 (Activities 15 to 17), so keep it short.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs decide the source type for each picture, then click Show. Point out that a name must be exact: not "the internet", but "North Sydney Council website". In Part 3, students list two different sources for their community services and two for their recreation activities. This previews Stop 8 (Activities 23 to 27).

Is it open all year?

🏊
1
What is your favourite place to relax?
2
How often do you go there?
3
Is it open all year?
Example: I go to the pool twice a week. It's open from October to April, so I can't go in winter.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs. Model with your own favourite place. Push how-often words (once a week, twice a month, every second Saturday) and opening dates (all year, from October to April, closed on Christmas Day). The project tables ask for "opening dates" and "frequency", and many outdoor pools in Sydney close in winter. This previews Stops 4 and 7 (Activities 13, 14 and 20).

New everyday talk: guess it!

Guess with your partner first. Then listen for these words today!
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs guess the meaning from the example sentence. You can hold the answers until after the Talk first conversation, or click now if the group needs support. All four are in the Julia and Nick conversation and in Activity 5. The other four new expressions (put you on hold, drop by, keep an eye out for, after hours) stay as a surprise for the worksheet.
